title: HIPPO: A Hierarchy-Preserving and Noise-Tolerant Pre-HLS Power Modeling Framework for FPGA
problem: Power estimation for custom FPGA accelerators from C/C++ requires invoking full EDA tool chains after high-level synthesis, creating large timing overheads that hinder early design optimization and limit iterative design space exploration.
motivation: Early power estimation enables faster design space exploration and optimization; pre-HLS analysis avoids expensive EDA tool invocation, enabling rapid prototyping of accelerator designs.
method: HIPPO operates directly on C/C++ programs with HLS pragmas, exploiting intrinsic code hierarchies (nested loops, operations). Multi-level power estimation aligns with different code hierarchies via: (1) code transformation to hardware-oriented control/dataflow graph, (2) hierarchy-preserving power modeling combining analytical and data-driven learning, (3) adaptive dataflow coarsening suppressing measurement noise.
key_novelty: Hierarchy-preserving power modeling framework operating pre-HLS on C/C++ code with multi-level estimation accuracy.
contributions: Pre-HLS power modeling avoiding full EDA tool chain

limitations: Evaluation limited to nested loop patterns; applicability to complex control flow unclear; validation against real silicon power measurements not shown.
primary_theme: Pre-HLS power estimation for FPGA accelerators
